bull_thesis:
The bull case is one experiment with a second asset underneath it. Annexon has no product revenue, so the case is whether the independent monitoring committee recommends that the pivotal ARCHER II trial of vonaprument has met its Month 15 goal in geographic atrophy, the advanced form of dry age-related macular degeneration in which patches of retina die and blind spots spread across central vision. That verdict is guided to the fourth quarter of 2026, which has about 45 days left, and as of 16 November 2026 it has not happened.

First, the trial measures the right thing. Regulators in the United States and Europe agreed it is judged on preventing a fifteen-letter loss of vision (three lines on an eye chart), not on slowing lesion growth. The two approved drugs were cleared on lesion growth and have never shown a benefit to sight, so a win makes vonaprument the only therapy shown to preserve vision in a disease affecting roughly a million Americans.

Second, the supporting evidence has a shape noise rarely produces. In the mid-stage trial monthly dosing cut the risk of fifteen-letter loss by 72% (p=0.006) and every-other-month dosing by 48%, a dose-response gradient; the pivotal trial doses every patient monthly, its 659 patients match the mid-stage population at baseline, retention is 90%, and blinded event rates are tracking the plan.

Third, the timing is forced by the visit schedule: every eligible patient has passed fifteen months of treatment, and no regulator clock, counterparty or financing sits in the path. The company is funded into 2028, so neither branch needs new money before the answer.

Fourth, the price now carries clearly worse odds than the evidence supports. The stock has fallen about 14% since the 9 November results, from $4.23 to about $3.63, on no company news and in a broad market and biotech sell-off. At $3.63 the market implies roughly a 20% chance of a win against our 38%, and a favourable recommendation would print near $9.50 inside the window, rising toward about $11 if the two United States sub-study analyses confirm in the first quarter of 2027. Short interest was last reported near 16.7% of the common, so a win meets a thin float.

Fifth, tanruprubart for Guillain-Barre syndrome, a sudden paralysing nerve disease with no approved disease-modifying therapy, showed a 2.4-fold improvement over placebo, and its United States application is guided for this quarter. The bull case needs: the recommendation inside the quarter, reading 'met' rather than 'continue'.
bear_thesis:
The bear case starts where the bull has to talk around: in mid-stage testing this drug did not measurably slow the disease. Lesion growth, that trial's own pre-specified main measure, missed; the vision benefit came from a secondary measure in a 270-patient trial, which is what a favourable draw among many outcomes can look like.

Second, the near bar was raised ten weeks before the data lock. On 12 August 2026 Month 24 was added as a second primary timepoint, splitting the statistical significance budget in an undisclosed way, and an affiliate filed a share-sale notice the next day.

Third, the failure branch is soft and the win is staged. The committee may simply recommend continuing to Month 24 - the single most likely outcome on our odds - which resets the price toward the asset floor in one session and then leaves nine months of fading option value. Even 'met' arrives without numbers, and the two United States sub-study analyses are not due until the first quarter of 2027. The 9 November release also dropped the explicit promise to report the assessment this quarter, saying only that the committee 'will assess' it.

Fourth, the company has been a steady seller of its own stock: about 12.3 million shares for $66.2 million net in the first nine months of 2026, plus 639,068 more for $2.7 million between 1 October and 9 November, into the October run. About $115.2 million of capacity remains and needs no new prospectus to use. That supply sits over any pre-verdict rally.

Fifth, the floor is thinner than it looks. Only about a third of it is cash; the rest is an asset mark on tanruprubart, still unfiled in the United States, whose launch funding becomes doubtful after an eye failure. $100 million of the $200 million credit facility is released only by the registrational milestones a miss would deny. And the one FDA binary in this funnel that resolved in October went to its loss leg and printed below cash. What would confirm the bear case: a 'continue to Month 24' recommendation, a futility call, or a quarter that ends with nothing said.

The data monitoring committee's Month 15 recommendation on ARCHER II in the fourth quarter of 2026. Every eligible patient has passed fifteen months of treatment, so the data lock follows mechanically from the visit schedule; no regulator clock, counterparty or financing can defer it. A 'met' recommendation changes the category - the only therapy shown to preserve sight in geographic atrophy - and prints first near $9.50, with the rest of the value earned on the first-quarter 2027 sub-study analyses. consensus_delta:
Where we disagree with the market can be measured. At about $3.63 the equity is worth about $746 million on 205.5 million share equivalents. In a miss the parts are worth roughly $330 to $470 million; on a 'met' recommendation about $1.95 billion. Solving for the odds the price carries gives about 20%, down from about 28.5% at $4.23 on 9 November. Nothing about the trial changed in between; the stock fell about 14% in five sessions on a market-wide and biotech sell-off (16 November alone: the stock down about 7%, the biotech index fund about 3%, the S&P 500 fund about 2%). Our estimate is 38%, so the gap is about 18 points - a disagreement about odds, not facts, and wider than a week ago.

Street readings that look wrong. First, the sell-side consensus target of about $15.29 (six buy, two hold, two sell; targets of $14 and $15 among them) is an approval-and-launch value that puts no weight on the miss branch and sits well above even a full win; it is not a cushion. Third, the market is now pricing this as sector beta into a dated binary, which is exactly the mispricing an event book exists to exploit.

Where we agree with the bears: the near bar rose in August, the soft 'continue' branch is the most likely outcome and is slow and corrosive to hold through, the company has been a steady seller of its own shares with $115.2 million of capacity left, and the floor is mostly an asset mark.
valley_of_death:
No maturity wall and no cash cliff before the answer: $213.4 million of cash and short-term investments at 30 September 2026 funds operations into 2028, past both Month 15 and Month 24; the $49.3 million term loan is not current.

What can go wrong in the next three to nine months, in order of importance:
1. A 'continue to Month 24' recommendation (47% on our odds): a one-session reset toward $1.60 to $2.30, then nine months of fading option value.
2. A 'met' recommendation followed by a weak United States sub-study in the first quarter of 2027, capping the re-rate well below the win value and complicating the American path.
3. Share supply into any rally: $115.2 million of at-the-market capacity, roughly 30 million shares at today's price, usable without a new prospectus. The company sold into the October run and may do so again.
4. The credit facility working against the company: $100 million is released only on registrational milestones a miss would deny.
5. The tanruprubart application slipping again or drawing an FDA refusal to file, eroding the two-thirds of the floor that is not cash.
6. Sector beta: the stock has moved -15%, +24% and -14% in a month on no trial information, and a verdict in the thin last week of December adds tape risk.

positioning_washout:
There is no forced selling by holders who must sell regardless of value: no dividend, no credit rating, no index deletion at this size, no price-linked covenant. The moves are discretionary trading around a binary and sector-wide flows.

Three phases so far. Capitulation by unwilling holders took the stock from about $5.00 in August to $3.41 on 16 October. Event traders then built in, to $4.23 on 9 November, while the company sold about 639,000 shares into the move. Since then a sector-wide sell-off has taken it back to about $3.63 on 16 November, roughly 5% below the chief executive's $3.83 open-market purchase and back near where the October run began - so the entry is cheaper for the same information.

The positioning fact that cuts our way: short interest was last reported at about 31.6 million shares, roughly 16.7% of the common, against institutional ownership above 90%, so a 'met' verdict would land on a thin, partly short float. The remaining supply risk is the company's own share-sale programme.
moderator_conclusion:
Buy now, sized for a one-session loss. Conviction 4, not 5.

The catalyst is real, inside its window and verified unfired today: the SEC record shows no filing since 9 November, the company has issued nothing since its results, and the registry is unchanged. The Month 15 committee verdict is guided to this quarter, about 45 days remain, and the data lock is forced by the visit schedule. The independent check's corrections from last week are adopted in full: the in-window win value is $9.50, not $11.00, and the company did sell meaningful stock into the readout.

The arithmetic has improved because the price fell on no information. At about $3.63 the probability-weighted value of $4.93 is about 36% above the price, clearing the 20% entry bar with room; gross asymmetry is about +162% against -53%, roughly 3 to 1; and the market implies about 20% win odds against our 38%. Even at 30% odds the weighted value is still about 20% above the price.

Why not a 5, in a funnel built to give 5s to this shape. First, the science: the bet rests on a vision signal that was a secondary measure in a 270-patient trial whose main measure missed, and the near bar rose in August. Second, the date is a company-guided quarter, not a statutory decision date, and the latest restatement no longer explicitly promises to report this quarter. Third, the floor is two-thirds asset judgement on an unfiled application, the conditional credit vanishes in the miss branch, and this funnel's only October FDA loss leg printed below cash. A 5 needs a firm date and a floor you can count on; this has a forced date and a floor you have to estimate.

The value case on its own is thin, and should be: at $3.63 against a $1.70 floor you pay about twice what the assets backstop, with about 53% at risk in the adverse branch - a value score of 2. The seat is earned on the event asymmetry alone. Size so that a 55% single-day fall is survivable, budget it inside the single FDA-cluster loss allowance, do not chase a pre-verdict rally (the company's share-sale programme will meet it), and watch the share count rather than for a prospectus supplement. Reassess at once if the quarter's end approaches with no word, or if the tanruprubart filing slips again.
interrogator_dossier:
# Annexon, Inc. (ANNX) - Event Dossier

Prepared 16 November 2026. Live price about $3.63 (16 November 2026, mid-afternoon New York time; down 7.3% on the day in a broad sell-off, with the S&P 500 fund down about 1.9% and the biotech index fund XBI down about 2.8%). Recent closes: $4.23 on 9 November, $4.21 on 10 November, $4.19 on 11 November, $3.97 on 12 November (4.5 million shares) and $3.92 on 13 November. That is a fall of about 14% in five sessions with no company news. Market value about $746 million on roughly 205.5 million share equivalents: 190,763,984 common shares at 5 November 2026 (quarterly report cover page) plus 14,745,093 shares issuable on pre-funded warrants struck at $0.001, which are economically shares already. Fifty-two-week range $2.54 to $7.18; 50-day average about $4.03, 200-day about $5.10.

This is not a business-quality note. Annexon is a clinical-stage biotechnology company with no product revenue, no margins and no franchise to defend, so every conventional quality and value measure looks poor by design. Three questions matter: whether one experiment reads out favourably inside this quarter, what a favourable read is worth inside the window, and what genuinely backstops the price if it does not.

## 0. WHAT CHANGED SINCE THE LAST LOOK (10 November 2026)

The trial has still not read out. The price fell; the facts did not move. Verified today against primary sources:

- The SEC filing record (read 16 November 2026 from the SEC's own data service): the most recent filings are still the quarterly report and the results current report, both 9 November 2026, plus a routine 5 November amendment to a passive-holder ownership notice. No current report announcing data, no registration statement, no prospectus supplement.
- The company's press-release feed: the latest release is still the 9 November third-quarter results. Nothing since.
- The trial registry entry NCT06510816 (read today through the registry's data service): unchanged since its 6 October 2026 update. Active, not recruiting, 659 patients actual, primary completion estimated 31 July 2027. It still does not date Month 15 on its own.
- Price: down from $4.23 to about $3.63 since the results release. One market-data note on 13 November could find no cause beyond a broker trimming its near-year loss estimates while keeping a buy rating and a $14 target. Today's leg is plainly market-wide. We read the whole move as positioning and sector beta, not information - the company itself is still blind to which arm the events fall in.

Two corrections from last week's independent check are now built into this record, because they were right:

1. Dilution was not minimal. The quarterly report shows 12,269,877 shares sold for about $66.2 million net under two at-the-market programmes (facilities for selling new shares gradually into the market) in the first nine months of 2026, about 6.4% of the common, and a further 639,068 shares for about $2.7 million net between 1 October and 9 November - that is, into the run from $3.41 to $4.23. About $115.2 million of capacity remains, which needs no new prospectus to use. The earlier warning sign ("watch for a prospectus supplement") was the wrong thing to watch; the right one is the share count in the next filing.
2. The in-window win value is about $9.50, not $11.00. A favourable committee recommendation is expected to print first around $9 to $10; the remainder needs the two United States sub-study analyses due in the first quarter of 2027, a second binary this quarter's verdict does not settle.

A third, softer point also stands: the 9 November release says only that the committee "will assess" the Month 15 endpoint this quarter. The commitment to report that assessment traces to the 12 August release ("the Company expects to report the DMC's assessment in the fourth quarter of 2026"). It has not been withdrawn, but it was not restated in those words.

## 1. NARRATIVE ARC (the event, not the franchise)

Annexon's platform blocks C1q, the trigger protein at the head of the classical complement cascade, the arm of the immune system that tags damaged tissue for removal. Vonaprument, formerly ANX007, is injected into the eye for geographic atrophy, the advanced form of dry age-related macular degeneration in which patches of retina die and blind spots spread across central vision. Tanruprubart, formerly ANX005, is given intravenously for Guillain-Barre syndrome, a sudden paralysing nerve disease with no approved disease-modifying therapy.

In 2023 the mid-stage ARCHER trial (270 patients) missed its own pre-specified main measure, slowing lesion growth, but showed a strong effect on a different one: the share of patients losing fifteen letters of vision, three lines on a standard eye chart. Management rebuilt the late-stage programme around vision and persuaded United States and European regulators to accept that as the registration endpoint; Europe granted priority-medicines support and the FDA granted Fast Track. The pivotal ARCHER II trial closed enrolment in July 2025 at 659 patients.

On 12 August 2026 management added Month 24 as a second primary timepoint. The trial can now win at either point - a genuine second shot - but the near bar probably rose (the statistical significance budget is split between the two timepoints, and the split is undisclosed) and a Month 15 miss now has a soft landing: the independent data monitoring committee may simply recommend continuing to Month 24. On 3 and 9 November the company set out the disclosure path: the committee assesses Month 15 this quarter; if it recommends the endpoint is met, it then evaluates the two pre-specified sub-studies, with results in the first quarter of 2027; otherwise it may recommend continuing to Month 24 (trial completion third quarter of 2027).

## 2. CLAIMS vs EVIDENCE (forensic)

| Management claim | What the evidence shows | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Month 15 committee assessment in the fourth quarter of 2026 | Restated 12 and 19 August, 24 September, 28 October, 3 and 9 November. Every eligible patient has passed fifteen months of treatment, so the data lock follows from the visit schedule. Unfired as of 16 November (SEC record, press feed). No independent registry date. About 45 days left in the quarter. | Supported by guidance and visit mechanics; no third-party date |
| The company will report the assessment this quarter | Said explicitly on 12 August; the 9 November release says only "will assess". | Likely, but the written commitment has thinned |
| The drug preserves vision | Mid-stage: monthly dosing cut the risk of fifteen-letter loss by 72% (89 patients, p=0.006); every-other-month dosing by 48% (92 patients, p=0.064). A dose-response gradient; the pivotal trial doses monthly. | Supported, with the caveat below |
| The drug treats the disease | The mid-stage trial's main measure, lesion growth, was not statistically significant. | Not supported; the core scientific risk |
| The pivotal trial is well powered | Blinded event rates tracking projections, 90% retention, more than 90% power cited at both timepoints. | Supported for power; silent on efficacy |
| Runway into 2028 | $213.4 million of cash and short-term investments at 30 September 2026; third-quarter operating cost $52.2 million; term loan carried at $49.3 million. | Supported |
| $200 million credit facility | $50 million drawn; $100 million released only on registrational milestones in the two lead programmes; $50 million at the lender's discretion. | Accurate but procyclical - the conditional money vanishes in the branch where it is needed |
| Tanruprubart United States application this quarter | Guided to the fourth quarter, with open-label United States and European data framed as answering the FDA's question on whether data gathered abroad apply to American patients. Not filed as of 16 November (no announcement). European application under review since January 2026. | Not yet delivered; the main non-cash floor input |

## 3. TONE & CONFIDENCE TRAJECTORY

Stable. Tone confident, timing never slipped. Against that, the August redesign was insurance bought ten weeks before a data lock, an affiliate filed notice of a share sale the next day, and the company kept selling stock through the October run. In its favour, the chief executive bought about $100,000 of stock in the open market at $3.83 on 24 September - the stock now trades about 5% below his price - and launch-oriented hiring continued into October.

## 4. GUIDANCE CREDIBILITY

Medium. Reliable on what management controls (enrolment ahead of plan and above target, cash runway, the eye timeline through six restatements); optimistic on what a regulator controls (the tanruprubart United States filing has slipped through 2026). The selling of shares into the readout, after describing the balance sheet as funded into 2028, is rational treasury management but does not sit perfectly with the confidence message.

## 5. ANALYST PRESSURE POINTS

1. How the significance budget is split between Month 15 and Month 24 - still undisclosed, and the single number that would let an outsider price the near bar.
2. Whether a "met" verdict on the overall study can coexist with one United States sub-study missing. The FDA wants two positive trials, so the single study was pre-split into two halves; one half missing would leave Europe intact and complicate the United States path.
3. Whether the company will use the remaining $115.2 million of share-sale capacity into any pre-verdict rally.
4. What it does for money after a miss, when $100 million of the credit facility goes out of reach.
Sell-side: six buy, two hold, two sell; average target about $15.29 (one broker at $14, another at $15). These are approval-and-launch values that put no weight on the miss branch.

## 6. RED FLAGS / GREEN FLAGS

Red flags:
- The mid-stage trial's main measure missed; the thesis rests on a secondary measure.
- Month 24 added on 12 August 2026 with the significance split undisclosed; affiliate share-sale notice 13 August.
- Continuous share sales: about $69 million net in 2026 to date, including into the October rally; $115.2 million of capacity left.
- The 9 November release dropped the explicit "report" language; the registry does not date Month 15.
- The fourth-quarter news is a committee recommendation, not a dataset; even a win leaves the sub-studies to the first quarter of 2027.
- Two-thirds of the floor is an asset mark on an unfiled United States application.
- The stock moved down 15%, up 24% and now down 14% in a month on no trial information - it trades as sector beta.
- Calibration warning from our own book: the one FDA binary in this funnel that resolved in October (EYPT) went to its loss leg and printed below cash. Loss-leg floors in this cluster should be treated as soft.

Green flags:
- Regulators on both sides of the Atlantic agreed the vision endpoint; European priority-medicines status and FDA Fast Track.
- Dose-response in the mid-stage trial; baseline-matched pivotal population; 90% retention; blinded event rates on plan.
- Timing mechanically forced: no agency clock, counterparty or financing in the path.
- $213.4 million of cash funds operations into 2028, past both readouts; no capital is needed on either branch before the answer.
- Chief executive open-market purchase at $3.83; no registration statement or prospectus supplement filed.

## 7. HIDDEN SIGNALS

The company is still blind to the arm-level data, so neither the share sales nor the restated wording carry efficacy information; they tell you about treasury practice and legal caution, not about the result. The disclosure path is fully specified in outcome terms (met, or continue), so whatever arrives will be readable on the day. The lending structure - growth tranches released only by registration milestones - remains a quiet signal that management did not expect to need failure-branch money.

## 8. THE VERIFIED DOWNSIDE FLOOR

What backstops the price if Month 15 fails:

- Net cash at the readout: about $116 million to $119 million, or about $0.57 a share. $213.4 million at 30 September 2026, less roughly $48 million of fourth-quarter cash use, plus a few million of share-sale proceeds, less the $49.3 million drawn secured loan, which ranks ahead of the equity. Contractual.
- Tanruprubart: $150 million to $250 million, about $0.73 to $1.22 a share. A late-stage Guillain-Barre winner (2.4-fold improvement over placebo on the standard disability scale), still unfiled in the United States, still awaiting a European opinion, with launch funding uncertain after an eye failure. Asset judgement, not a payout.
- Oral ANX1502 and platform residual: about $0.05 to $0.10 a share.

Sum about $1.40 to $1.95; we carry $1.70 (independently confirmed last week; remaining share-sale capacity used at a post-miss $2.00 to $2.30 would add to, not eat, this floor). Branch marks: a miss reported as "continue to Month 24" near $2.30 (floor plus a residual Month 24 option); a clean failure or futility call near $1.60. Given the EYPT print, treat these as ceilings on a loss-leg print rather than hard floors. The fifty-two-week low of $2.54 was set with the eye option alive and supports nothing.

## 9. CAPITAL-ALLOCATION VERDICT (for the director)

Trajectory: stable. The catalyst is live, unfired and inside its quarter; the price has fallen about 14% on no information, which widens the edge rather than signalling anything.

Moat and secular threat do not apply: there is no product revenue to protect.

Outcome tree from $3.63, probabilities unchanged because nothing about efficacy has changed: about 38% a "met" recommendation printing near $9.50 inside the window; about 47% a recommendation to continue to Month 24, near $2.30; about 15% a clean failure, near $1.60. Probability-weighted value about $4.93, roughly 36% above the price. Gross upside about +162% to $9.50 against about -53% to the $1.70 floor, about 3.0 to 1. The price now implies roughly a 20% chance of a win against our 38% (about 28.5% at $4.23 on the corrected $9.50 win value). Even at 30% odds the weighted value is about $4.34, roughly +20%.

The single most important thing to weigh: the adverse outcome arrives in one session and cannot be traded out of, the floor is two-thirds asset judgement, and the "dated" catalyst is a company-guided quarter forced by the visit schedule, not a statutory decision date. Size so that a 55% single-day fall in the position is survivable.
